root_cause.text: In `drivers/infiniband/ulp/srp/ib_srp.c`, `srp_process_rsp()` used the target-supplied `resp_data_len` to compute the sense-data source offset without verifying that `sizeof(*rsp) + resp_data_len + sense_data_len` was within `wc->byte_len`, allowing an SRP target to make the kernel read past the received RDMA buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `srp_process_rsp()` to take `byte_len` and adds `if (sizeof(*rsp) + (u64)resp_len + sense_len <= byte_len)` before `memcpy()`, with the comment explicitly stating that otherwise “the copy source would run past the receive buffer”; the CVE text also says `resp_data_len` “is never checked against the number of bytes actually received (wc->byte_len)”.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `srp_process_rsp()` to take `byte_len` and adds `if (sizeof(*rsp) + (u64)resp_len + sense_len <= byte_len)` before `memcpy()`, with the comment explicitly stating that otherwise “the copy source would run past the receive buffer”; the CVE text also says `resp_data_len` “is never checked against the number of bytes actually received (wc->byte_len)”.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend `srp_process_rsp` to accept the received byte length so response handling can account for the actual packet size.
intent_record.what: The function `srp_process_rsp` had its signature changed from taking two arguments (`struct srp_rdma_ch *ch, struct srp_rsp *rsp`) to taking three arguments by adding a `u32 byte_len` parameter. No other code in the hunk is modified.
intent_record.how: At runtime, callers of `srp_process_rsp` can now pass the received byte length of the response, allowing the function to make processing decisions based on the actual size of the incoming buffer. This enables handling of variable-length or truncated responses more safely or accurately.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a bounds check to prevent out-of-bounds sense data reads from truncated SRP responses and log the error instead of copying invalid data.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct memcpy of SCSI sense data with local variables for resp_data_len and sense_data_len, adds a bounds check against byte_len before copying, and emits an error log instead of copying when the sense data would be truncated; the copy length is also changed to min(sense_len, SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the handler now verifies that the complete sense region is present in the received response before accessing it, preventing an out-of-bounds read from the receive buffer. If the response is truncated, it skips copying the sense data and logs an error, avoiding memory corruption or invalid reads while preserving safe handling of the command result.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pass the received buffer length into SRP response handling so response processing can use the actual byte count.
intent_record.what: In `srp_recv_done()`, the call to `srp_process_rsp()` was changed from passing two arguments (`ch`, `iu->buf`) to passing three arguments (`ch`, `iu->buf`, `wc->byte_len`).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the response-processing function now receives the actual received byte length from the completion work request, allowing it to validate or interpret the incoming SRP response based on the full packet size instead of only the buffer pointer.

grouping_result.intent: Pass the received buffer length into SRP response handling so response processing can use the actual byte count.

consistency_review.core_intent: Update SRP response processing to use the actual received byte length and safely validate response buffers.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they make `srp_process_rsp()` use the actual received byte length and add bounds checking to prevent out-of-bounds reads when processing target-supplied response and sense data lengths.

new file mode 100644
index 00000
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable logic is present in `srp_process_rsp()`. The code does `memcpy(scmnd->sense_buffer, rsp->data + be32_to_cpu(rsp->resp_data_len), min_t(int, be32_to_cpu(rsp->sense_data_len), SCSI_SENSE_BUFFERSIZE));` when `rsp->flags & SRP_RSP_FLAG_SNSVALID` is set. This directly uses the target-controlled `resp_data_len` as an offset into `rsp->data` without any check that `sizeof(*rsp) + resp_data_len + sense_data_len` stays within the received buffer. There is no bounds check against `wc->byte_len` (or any equivalent length validation) in this function, so the unsafe read past the RDMA buffer is present. The fix is not present because there is no validation before the memcpy; the code only limits the copy length with `min_t(...)`, which does not constrain the source offset or total accessed size.
